body: Most likely `$app->terminate()` was never called during the test runtime.
I'm having the same issue here. Is there any way to test a terminable middleware?
Sorry, but this is not a forum. We do have a forum, so please ask there. I'm sure there will be lots of people who can help you there. :)

So, bug reporting should be handled in the forums?

I consider it a bug, because the existence of `WithoutMiddleware` implies middleware will be executed if this trait is not included.

Terminable middleware is not executed correctly when doing things like `$this->post('foo')`. This is either a bug or unexpected behavior (since other middleware is executed just fine).

It can be fixed by contributing to this repository (by code or by clarifying the non-obvious behavior in the docs).

I reported it, @rafaelbeckel has the same _issue_ (so having an _issue_ on a GitHub repo to me seems like the exact right place to discuss this until it is resolved).

Why in your opinion shouldn't it be discussed/resolved here? I am not asking for a tutorial to write integration tests ...

I am confused. Please clarify your thinking behind "forum is the right place to put this".
You're going to have to provide more information then. Where are you declaring this middleware?
Middleware inside controllers for example DO NOT terminate. It's simply not supported.

The middleware is `App\Http\Middleware\Test`, so it is in `app/Http/Middleware/Test.php`.

I use it in the Kernel (`app\Http\Kernel.php`) like so:

``` php
<?php namespace App\Http;

class Kernel extends HttpKernel
{
    /**
     * The application's global HTTP middleware stack.
     *
     * @var array
     */
    protected $middleware = [
        \Illuminate\Foundation\Http\Middleware\CheckForMaintenanceMode::class,
        \Illuminate\Cookie\Middleware\EncryptCookies::class,
        \Illuminate\Cookie\Middleware\AddQueuedCookiesToResponse::class,
        \Illuminate\Session\Middleware\StartSession::class,
        \Illuminate\View\Middleware\ShareErrorsFromSession::class,

        /**
         * Application specific middleware...
         */
        Middleware\Test::class,
    ];
```

Pretty standard and right out of the docs.

The middleware works everywhere except the testing environment (phpunit).
Hmmm, ok. Thanks for providing that.
Thanks. Let me know if I can help any further to resolve this.
We never call the send method when testing.
Isn't a call to $this->visit('/') a normal http request to the index.php file?

> Isn't a call to $this->visit('/') a normal http request to the index.php file?

No?
@rafaelbeckel No. Instead of an actual HTTP request, the instance of `Symfony\HttpFoundation\Request` gets dispatched to the router directly, because it is substantially faster.
OK. I just read the call() implementation now. Sorry for the dumb question. Should have read it before posting. ;)
